title: Kyoto cherry blossom

data.source: Kyoto full-flowering dates of Prunus jamasakura, 812 to 2010 (Aono and Kazui 2008; Aono and Saito 2010), NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology, study 26430
data.licence: Public (NOAA/WDS Paleoclimatology archive; free to use with citation)

prediction: With q learned on the first half of the recorded springs, the seed rule predicts the next flowering day with an RMSE at least 2% below the best of the 30-spring normal, the running mean, persistence and a line through the last 100 springs.
baseline: The mean of the last 30 recorded springs (the climate normal), the running mean, persistence, and a straight line through the last 100 recorded springs.
why: The seed rule and the best plain forecast came out within 2% of each other. A fading memory of past springs is the weather service's moving normal in other words.
